about: Going back to look at a thing: which viewpoint would sharpen where it is, and when none would.

room.comment: A plain mapped room with a thing or two in it and nothing to explore.

closet.comment: A cupboard shut off from the room. Nothing inside it can be looked at from anywhere the rover can walk to.

faraway.comment: Mapped floor down the left, and unmapped ground stretching away. A thing out in that ground cannot be approached closer than three metres.

scenarios.name: a thing whose distance nobody has measured is worth going to see
scenarios.why: Six looks and not one range: it is placed by crossing bearings alone, and a viewpoint the depth camera can work from is the thing that would settle it.

scenarios.name: a thing already placed as well as this rover can place anything
scenarios.why: Eight centimetres is better than the acceptance run's best tape-measured pair. There is nothing left to win, and proposing a drive for it would be the scorer inventing work.

scenarios.name: the worse placed of two things is the one to go and look at
scenarios.why: Both are reachable and both would improve; the ranking has to follow how badly each is placed rather than which is nearer.

scenarios.name: a thing shut in a cupboard is refused, not forgotten
scenarios.why: There is nowhere to stand that can see it. That has to appear in the record as a refusal with a reason, because a thing that is silently never considered looks exactly like a thing nothing wanted.

scenarios.name: a thing the rover cannot get within three metres of is refused by the band
scenarios.why: The geometry was accepted between half a metre and two and a half. A look from further out is not forbidden by physics, it is outside what anybody has checked -- and the refusal says the distance.

scenarios.name: with the perception loop stopped, a thing needing a range is refused
scenarios.why: The distance is the whole point of that goal, and the camera that measures it is reached through the loop that is not running.

scenarios.name: a thing that has been ranged is not refused for the depth camera
scenarios.why: The other side of the same rule: a second bearing needs no depth camera, so a stopped loop is not a reason to refuse it.

scenarios.name: a placement from a map that has been replaced is not driven to
scenarios.why: Its coordinates belong to a map that no longer exists. The world state keeps such a thing so it can be recognised again, not so the rover can drive to where it used to be.

scenarios.name: a thing seen once and never placed is not proposed at all
scenarios.why: One bearing is a direction and not a position, so there is nowhere to plan a viewpoint around. What that thing needs is for the rover to be somewhere else, which is what exploring is for.

scenarios.name: when the height is a guess, the gain is halved and says so
scenarios.why: The validated envelope covers tilt zero and tilt +20, and a thing whose height above the floor is uncertain to a metre could need either. Charging for the ignorance is the conservative direction; pretending to know is the other one.

scenarios.name: the same thing with a known height is worth twice as much
scenarios.why: The pair to the case above, so that the discount is visible as a difference rather than asserted.

scenarios.name: a marginal improvement is not worth disturbing the rover for
scenarios.why: Twelve centimetres off a placement that is already at fourteen. Being reachable and safe is not a reason to drive.

scenarios.name: two places to stand are offered when they are a real choice
scenarios.why: The good viewpoint and the cheap one are a trade, and the trade belongs to the scorer. A generator that picked for it would be a scorer nobody could see.
